fix(table): swap the box a headerless table draws with (rich-table-6uy.6)

Python Rich substitutes the box itself when a table has no header — five of
the nineteen constants map to a plainer kin, the default HEAVY_HEAD among
them — and this port did not, so `showHeader: false` drew heavy header glyphs
on the top border of an otherwise light frame.

`Box.plainHeaded()` stands beside `substitute()` rather than joining its
options bag: one asks what the platform can draw, the other what the table
contains, and nothing correlates them.

The relation is keyed on the grid rather than on object identity as the
reference's dict is. A Box is wholly determined by its grid, so two boxes
carrying one grid must answer alike — and `safeSubstitute` already builds such
a box, a fresh instance with an unchanged grid, which identity keying would
have silently failed to substitute.

Also collapses the asciiOnly ternary at the callsite: `substitute` already
returns the receiver when the flag is off, so the outer branch was a second
place deciding one thing.

Pinned by the `no-header-no-footer` configuration added to the golden frame
sweep, regenerated from Python Rich — all 38 pre-existing blocks reproduce
byte-for-byte, 19 are new. Both gates proven to fail by isolated revert:
dropping the swap reddens the golden, and identity keying reddens only the
aliasing unit test, which is what it is there for.

fix(table): parse markup at the one crossing that makes cell text (rich-table-6uy.5) (#96)

* fix(table): parse markup at the one crossing that makes cell text (rich-table-6uy.5)

`addRow("[red]Solo[/red]: A Star Wars Story")` put the tags on the terminal.
The cause was not one missing parse but five separate ones: cells, headers,
footers, the title and the caption each built their own `RichText` straight
from the constructor, which by design does not parse markup. One rule, five
homes, absent from all five.

So the fix is a consolidation rather than five edits. `toCellText` is now the
single crossing every one of those positions goes through, and markup parsing
lives there once. Parsing is unconditional because that is what the reference
does — Rich's `Console.__init__` declares `markup: bool = True` and all five
positions reach the wire through `Console.render_str` — not because it was the
smaller branch. `toRenderable` loses its `instanceof RichText` arm: `RichText`
implements `Renderable`, so it already leaves through the renderable arm
untouched.

Two further defects surfaced, and both had to be fixed for the parse to mean
anything:

- `_renderTitle` rendered `text.plain`, reading the characters and dropping
  every span attached to them. Parsing without this would have been strictly
  worse than the bug: the tags would vanish and the colour would silently never
  appear. It now renders the content's own segments over the table's title
  style as the base, which is what the reference emits — `\e[3;31m` for a
  `[red]` title in an italic table title, italic and red rather than either
  one. The crop/pad fork went with it; `adjustLineLength` handles both by value.
- `_naturalWidth` measured the raw cell value, so a column sized itself to
  `[red]Solo[/red]` — fifteen cells for four cells of text. Measurement now
  asks the same crossing that renders it what the text is.

Verified against Python Rich itself, not against reasoning about it. The
docs/tables.md flagship example rendered at width 88 now matches the reference
character for character on six of seven lines, including both markup-bearing
rows. The seventh is a wrapping difference with no markup in it, reproduced
with none anywhere and filed as rich-table-6uy.7.

Each of the three gates was proven to go red, in isolation: dropping the parse
fails all six markup tests; flattening the title back to `.plain` fails exactly
Title and Caption; measuring the raw value again fails exactly the width test.

.4's golden fixture is untouched, as its own comment predicted — its cells are
plain digits precisely so this change could not move a frame in it.

* fix(table): stamp each cell once, and render titles the reference's way

Four defects the review surfaced, three of which this branch introduced.

Cells were converted twice per render — `_naturalWidth` and `_renderRow` each
resolved the raw value independently, which is two authorities on what a cell
is. They disagreed: a `Panel` stringifies to `[object Object]`, which the tag
pattern matches whole, so markup-parsing it in the sizing path returned empty
text and measured the column as zero. `addRow` now resolves each cell through
`toRenderable` once and stores `Renderable[]`, so both consumers read one
stamped value and re-parsing is unrepresentable rather than merely avoided.
Measured on a 500x8 table: 15.12 ms/render back to 10.52, against a pre-branch
baseline of 10.39. The cost is that `MarkupError` now surfaces at `addRow`
rather than lazily at render — a stated divergence from the reference, taken
because the error still surfaces with the same message and now points at the
call holding the bad string.

Sizing a cell that draws itself still stringifies rather than measures it, so a
`Panel` contributes a wrong non-zero width. That gap is pre-existing and stays:
`_columnDemands` carries no `RenderOptions`, so `Measurement.get` is not
reachable from there.

`_renderTitle` took only the first line, so a title carrying a newline lost
everything after it silently. The reference renders every line, verified by
running it — `"Line one\nLine two"` now emits both, centered, matching the
reference character for character. It also emitted a blank line for `title: ""`
where the reference emits none; the loop disposes of that too.

`titleJustify` was not the owner of its own alignment. A `RichText` carrying its
own `justify` pads itself to the full width inside `render`, collapsing the gap
and silently outvoting the table's option. The title now renders from a copy
with `justify` cleared.

Not fixed here, filed as rich-markup-sec: this port's tag grammar accepts
`[A-Z]` where the reference's accepts only `[a-z#/@]`, so `[INFO]` is eaten as
a tag here and printed literally there. That is a `core/markup` defect reaching
every `Console.print`, pre-existing and merely made reachable from a table cell
by this branch. Narrowing the class locally passes all 2259 tests unchanged,
which is the finding rather than the fix — the grammar is unpinned, and it
deserves the reference audit rich-table-6uy.3 gave the box data.

* fix(table): leave no phantom column when a cell's markup is malformed

Parsing at the border gave `addRow` a way to throw that it did not have
before, and the column auto-create loop ran ahead of the parse — so
`addRow("ok", "[/bad]")` on a one-column table raised `MarkupError` with a
second, empty column already committed. A caller that caught the error and
retried with valid data inherited the phantom.

Resolving the cells before the loop makes `addRow` all-or-nothing. The
operations are unchanged and still all run; only their order moved, so there
is no rollback path and no try/catch to keep correct.

The eager throw is a deliberate divergence — Rich stores the raw string and
raises the same `MarkupError` lazily at print time — so both halves are now
pinned: that `addRow("[/bad]")` throws where this port parses, and that the
failed call leaves the column list untouched. Each was proven to fail by an
isolated revert.

* fix(table): consult the plugin registry at the cell crossing

`core/markup.ts` exports two functions that turn markup into `RichText`, and
this file imported the plain `render` under the name `renderMarkup` — as
`console.ts` and `prompt.ts` still do. A tag registered on
`globalMarkupRegistry`, which `examples/rich-markup-plugins` does, therefore
degraded silently inside every table cell, header, footer, title and caption:
tag consumed, content unstyled, nothing reported.

The real `renderMarkup` is a strict superset. Both of its early exits — no `[`
in the string, and zero paired plugin tags — delegate to `render` with the same
base style and the same emoji default. Output was verified identical across
eleven markup shapes, malformed input raises the same `MarkupError`, and a
500x8 table showed no regression (plain 36.8ms -> 35.2ms, `[red]v[/red]`
57.4ms -> 53.6ms, median of ten runs). So this costs nothing a caller who
registers nothing can observe.

No registry threaded through `TableOptions`: that would be a mode with no
reference behaviour to define, and the global registry is the one `progress.ts`
already reads.

`toCellText`'s comment said those five positions reach the wire through
`Console.render_str`, meaning Rich's; it read as this port's `console.ts`. It
names Rich now.

The remaining console.ts/prompt.ts split is filed as rich-markup-pcp.

* test(table): pin the eager markup throw at every position that carries it

Parsing at the border moved the `MarkupError` from render time to the call that
supplies the string, and only the cell position was held still. The other four
convert just as eagerly — `Column`'s constructor for header and footer,
`Table`'s for title and caption — so a constructor that could not throw before
this branch can now throw at four sites with nothing pinning it.

Checked against the reference per position: Rich raises the same error from all
five, at print time. The divergence is uniformly when, never whether. The first
probe of that claim reported "no throw" for a title, because a table with no
columns renders no title and so never parsed it; a table with a row present
throws for every position.

One `it.each` rather than a test per site, matching the positional test a screen
above it and its stated reason — one rule with five call sites is one assertion
driven by five values. The single-position test it replaces is gone, so five
positions are now covered by fewer bodies than one had. Reverting any one
position to an unparsed `RichText` turns exactly that row red and no other.

No atomicity test for `addColumn`: `new Column(...)` already throws before the
push, so there is no defect there to pin.

* fix(table): clear end on a caller's RichText, not just on parsed markup

`title?: string | RichText` documents two input shapes and `toCellText` stamped
only one of them: the `instanceof RichText` early return handed the object back
untouched, so a `RichText` carrying its default `end` of "\n" kept it. An empty
one then drew a full-width blank line above the frame — the same stray line this
branch already removed for `title: ""`, still reachable through the other half
of the union, and at the bottom of the frame for `caption`.

The reference emits no line for either shape, so this was a divergence rather
than a preference.

The hole was the early return itself, not a step it forgot. Clearing `end` is an
operation every path owes; the input shape decides only how the `RichText` is
obtained. One branch now picks between `copy()` and a parse, and the stamp runs
after it unconditionally. The copy is what keeps the clear from reaching back
into the caller's object, and it carries style, justify, overflow, tabSize,
noWrap and the spans, so a title's own justify still arrives for `titleJustify`
to outrank.

`text.ts` is left alone deliberately. Its empty-text branch yields `end`
unguarded where the non-empty branch suppresses a bare "\n", which looks like
the deeper cause but is what makes `console.print(new RichText(""))` emit a
blank line at all. `end = ""` is how a caller says "fragment, not line", and the
table's crossing is where that already gets said.

The empty-content test now runs over both shapes in both positions, and compares
the whole frame: it read only the first line before, which is why the caption
half could not have been caught. Reverting the early return turns exactly the
two RichText rows red.

* fix(table): stop re-stamping a footer that was stamped at its column

Giving `toCellText` a `copy()` arm in f3cf43df turned the footer row's
`toCellText(c.footer)` from a pass-through into an allocation per column per
render — `c.footer` is already a resolved `RichText`, stamped once in the
`Column` constructor, so the copy bought nothing. The header line directly above
reuses its stored instance, and the two had no reason to differ.

Measured on a 500x8 table with a footer on every column, built once and
re-rendered: 4.28ms -> 4.16ms, median of 20 passes after 3 warmups. Modest, and
bounded by column count rather than row count; the consistency was the larger
half.

The absent case routes back through `toCellText` rather than spelling
`new RichText("", { end: "" })` at this site, so the rule that table content
carries no line ending stays at the crossing that owns it. It is also what the
data rows a few lines up already do for a missing cell.

A mixed table — one column with a footer, one without — was reachable through
no test. It is pinned now against the reference, character for character.
Sabotaging the absent arm's content reddens that test and only that test;
dropping the cell entirely reddens nothing, because `_renderRow` pads a short
list, so the test's comment claims the content and not the padding.
